## K12 · K12-full-fill-ring — At the full fill the 2048-page trace ring overflows; the measured full-size phases

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 3

Decision references: 86d2ec1c0

Evidence: Ring = 8192 pages (32 MiB, 1,048,576 records, ~2x rv32's 535,673), K12's change with scheduling.md's residual; dropped 0, no window, no per-case size. The budget stands (full-fill numbers within 5% of the scaled estimates); the owner walk's narrow reader is timed early on scratch against its 8 ms (stop if over 12). wait_arm is GATE1's fix. Written in budgets.md (86d2ec1c0) and the K12 brief.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `46a4544e07ca1a8773f3d110c602e579` · 2026-10-01T00:14:42Z

> GATE1's round-2 bisect (./.wash/local/GATE1-r10-bisect.md, 'Round 2') measured the gate at its ruled full fill: a 5,900-page lease reaches 4,091 endpoints and ends on the table-full refusal, so the minimum is ~5,700 pages. Two rulings needed. (1) The trace ring: 2048 pages (done in K12 step 0) is not enough at the full fill. rv64 needs 491,236 records (4096 pages drop 0); rv32 needs 535,673 (4096 pages drop 11,385). So the ring needs about 4,200+ pages, e.g. 8192 (32 MiB) on a 256 MiB machine with the fill's ~23 MiB lease. Rule the size (or another approach that keeps 'dropped 0' and no hidden window), and whether it's K12's change or GATE1's. (2) For K12's budget, confirm it against the measured full-size phases, rv64 H|D (rv32): total 251|102 ms (270|110); sweep 150.3|4.6; owner walk 37.4; own handle close 31.6; release_all_memory 10.8; process_ending 7.8; notice walk 6; deferred frees 3.7. Per own endpoint, all-in 17.8 µs (rv32 19.4). Your 25 ms budget assumes ~2 µs per endpoint for the owner walk and frees, and 2 ms for own tables: do these numbers change the stop rule or the plan? Also: a full fill arms in ~60 s virtual, so GATE1's wait_arm cap grows (GATE1's own fix).

### Architect · Answer

Event: `8f13bd420e008ac745ca2a28ab09bf11` · 2026-10-01T00:16:32Z

> (1) Ring: trace::PAGES = 8192 (32 MiB, 1,048,576 records). That is about 2x rv32's 535,673. The run grows as fills arm more slowly and as K12 moves timing, so 4608 is too thin. A power of two is one constant. Every trace case runs at the default 256 MiB, and the gate's two leases (~12K pages) plus 8K for the ring fit in 64K. It is test-only. The rules stay: dropped 0, no window, no per-case size (GATE1-composed-r10 ruling 3). It is K12's change, as step 0 was: K12 owns the trace module and scheduling.md "Residual risks" ("2 MiB less RAM" becomes 32 MiB in the same commit). Amend e03b8940c or follow it with one commit. GATE1 may carry 8192 on scratch until then.
> 
> (2) Budget: it stands, and so do the stop rule and the plan. The full-fill numbers match the brief's scaled estimates within 5% (rv32 H): own tables ~35 → 34.8, owner walk + frees ~43 → 44.3, release_all_memory 10.5, process_ending 8.2, notice walk 6.2. The sweep was 162 ms at the full neighbour, and the chain walk replaces it (0.5 ms). The 25 ms keeps the brief's per-object targets: 4,096 slots at ~0.4 µs (2 ms) and 4,091 endpoints at ~2 µs (8 ms), ~2.5 µs per own endpoint in all, against 19.4 µs today. The fixed lines (process_ending 8, walks 2, frames 1.5, rest 3) leave nothing for slack, so the endpoints line is the risk. Recommendation, not a change: the owner walk's narrow reader doesn't depend on the chains, so K12 can time it on scratch early. A miss (>12 ms, 50% over) then trips the stop rule before step 2 is fully sunk.
> 
> (3) wait_arm: agreed, GATE1's own fix; size it from the measured ~60 s with margin.
> 
> Written: budgets.md Residual risks now gives the full-fill measurement (102/251 ms rv64, 18 µs per endpoint) in 86d2ec1c0. The K12 brief (step 0 = 8192, measured row) and GATE1-composed-r10-architect.md are updated. Decision refs for the resolve: 86d2ec1c0.
